External evaluator's review of the manua: Chance agreement (Pe, from the distribution of tag labels)

The external evaluator reviewed 25 annotated posts and left comments on the annotations. I treated each comment as one candidate disagreement. A comment was counted as a disagreement only when the evaluator stated or clearly implied that an annotation should change (a wrong label, a wrong clause structure, a missing or extra tag, or a missing bracket). Repeated pointers such as "See previous comment" were counted separately, because each refers to a different tag. Comments that did not contest an annotation were not counted: remarks on the post author's grammar, wording or register, a typo in the post, agreement or uncertainty, and clarification queries in which the evaluator asked about a tag without stating that it was wrong. Posts which held a single comment confirming the annotation counted as containing no disagreements. Tags were counted with the regular expressions used in the analysis code (pronoun tags and sentence brackets). Because the evaluator reviewed existing annotations rather than annotating the posts independently, kappa is approximate: chance agreement was estimated from the distribution of the 67 tag labels, assuming both annotators would use them in the same proportions. Agreement refers to the annotation before disagreements were resolved.
